title: Alternaria early blight disease in round potato / Irish potato

Header: Alternaria early blight disease in round potato / Irish potato
Alternaria solani Bakajani wahi in Swahili

Prevention: Use disease-free seeds and a tolerant variety such as
Do not rotate with tomato, sweet pepper, eggplant, nightshade
Remove plant debris after harvest as it harbours the disease.
However, if no major insect pests or diseases are in your crop, then leave residues to improve soil, and reduce water loss
Avoid crowded plants as this favours disease multiplication (space at least 60 x 60cm).
Avoid overhead irrigation as this can splash the disease from plant to plant
Monitoring: This is a fungal disease, also called tuber blight
During the warm wet season, the disease is most serious; monitor potato plants every 2 to 3 days.
Search for small dark brown to black spots on the lower shaded leaves and stems.
The spots are surrounded by concentric rings of leathery tissue.
Early blight lesions are zonate with a definite margin, whereas late blight lesions are never zonate and do not have definite margin
When 2-3 leaves are affected per 20 plants, consider action
Tuber lesions are dry, dark and pressed into the tuber surface, with the underlying flesh turning dry, brown
Direct Control: Prevention is the most powerful measure.
Direct control is difficult and often too late
Remove all affected leaves, and discard them away from the field.
Use polythene bags to transport them out of the field, as you otherwise spread the disease.
Soak pounded 1kg neem tree leaves in 5L of water for 24 hrs and spray the fluid after mixing it with water in a 2:1 ratio.
A tablespoon of soap is added to the mixture
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Farmers are not allowed to buy and/or use

Multisite mode of action, thus resistance unlikely.
